title: WPSB/418/2026 of VIJENDRA PRATAP SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010117222026
2026:UHC:5530-DB
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
July 08, 2026
Writ Petition (S/B) No.418 of 2025
Dr. Vijendra Pratap Singh ----Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & Others ----Respondents
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Yogesh Kumar Pacholia, learned counsel for the petitioner
Mr. Puran Singh Bisht, learned Chief Standing Counsel with Mr. J.C. Pande, learned
Standing Counsel and Mr. M.S. Bisht, learned Brief Holder for the State.
JUDGMENT : (per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.)
1. The petitioner, who is presently holding the post of
Veterinary Officer, is aggrieved by the transfer order dated
30.06.2026, whereby he has been transferred from
Government Veterinary Hospital, Subhash Nagar, Dehradun to
Sheep Breeding Farm, Kedarkantha, District Chamoli.
2. The case of the petitioner is that his name has been
wrongly included in the eligibility list prepared under Section 8
of the Uttarakhand Annual Transfer For Public Servants Act,
2017 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act'). It is submitted
that the petitioner has not completed 04 years of service at
the present place of posting i.e. Subhash Nagar, Dehradun.
1

UKHC010117222026
2026:UHC:5530-DB
According to the petitioner, the total service rendered by him
at Subhash Nagar, Dehradun, which is an accessible place, is
03 years and 03 months only, and therefore he is not covered
by Section 8 of the Act. It is stated that the petitioner was
transferred to Veterinary Hospital, Subhash Nagar, Dehradun,
vide order dated 07.01.2022, however, the said order was
challenged by one Rajiv Mohan Sharma by way of Writ Petition
(S/B) No.150/2022 and, vide order dated 04.04.2022, this
Court stayed the effect and operation of the order dated
07.01.2022. Consequently, the Department, vide its order
dated 09.05.2022, directed the petitioner to join at the
Directorate of Animal Husbandry and the petitioner continued
there until the writ petition was dismissed and the order of his
attachment was revoked by order dated 09.01.2023. He
submits that the said period has to be excluded while counting
the service rendered at accessible place. It is further
submitted that there are several other government employees
who have rendered virtually no service at remote place. It is
further submitted that the Government is adopting pick and
choose policy in effecting transfers inasmuch as the persons
named in paragraph 21 have remained posted at accessible
place for a much longer period.
3. Learned State Counsel has placed on record the
2

UKHC010117222026
2026:UHC:5530-DB
instructions received from the Directorate and, according to
which, the Department has rightly calculated the period of
service of the petitioner at an accessible place. It is further
stated that the Department is acting strictly in accordance
with the Transfer Policy and the allegation of 'pick and choose'
has been denied. It has further been stated that in the option
form, the petitioner had not given any option for transfer at an
accessible place and, consequently the options given by the
petitioner could not be accepted.
4. Section 8 of the Act is as follows:-
"The maximum ceiling of compulsory transfer from accessible
area to remote area shall be as follows, namely: -
The compulsory transfer from accessible area to
remote area shall be made up to the limit of availability of
vacancies in remote areas in the concerned cadre. The
counting of eligible employees for such transfers shall be
done in order of total service rendered in accessible area
during the whole service period, i.e., such employees who
have completed more than 04 years posting in accessible
area or whose total service in accessible area during the
whole service period has been more than 10 years and who
do not fall under any exemption shall be identified for
transfer upto the limit of availability of vacancies in remote
areas of concerned cadre by placing them in descending
order according to their total period of posting in accessible
area."
5. The provision clearly states that counting of eligible
employees for transfer shall be done in order of total service
3

UKHC010117222026
2026:UHC:5530-DB
rendered in accessible place during the whole service period,
i.e., such employee who have completed more than 04 years
posting in accessible area or whose total service in accessible
area during the whole service period has been more than 10
years.
6. In the instant case, the Department has transferred
the petitioner for the reason that he had completed more than
04 years of posting in accessible area. The provision does not
state that only the period at a specified accessible place has to
be counted but it is the whole service period which is relevant.
The attachment of the petitioner at the Directorate, i.e. at the
same place, while interim order was in operation in writ
petition filed by Rajiv Mohan Sharma, would therefore, also
count while reckoning the total service rendered at an
accessible place. Therefore, we find no force in the
submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that the
petitioner had not rendered the prescribed 04 years period of
service at an accessible area and, therefore, would not be
covered by Section 8 of the Act.
7. As regards the second contention, we find that
although the petitioner has mentioned name of certain
employees and the duration of their service at accessible
4

UKHC010117222026
2026:UHC:5530-DB
areas but it has not been stated anywhere in the writ petition
that what action has been taken by the State Government in
relation to the said Officers. As such, we also do not find any
force in the second submission.
8. Moreover, transfer is an exigency of service. The
petitioner, who has already completed maximum period of
service at an accessible place, does not have any equity in his
favour.
9. Consequently, we decline to interfere with the
transfer order. Writ petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
 (MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
